newsitem.title: UK: Henderson rejects TI's Forsheda bid.
newsitem.headline: Henderson rejects TI's Forsheda bid.

text.p: Henderson Investors, which through several of its investment funds controls nearly 13 percent of Sweden's Forsheda engineering company, said on Friday it has rejected a 189 million stg takeover bid by TI Group.

"While the TI bid represents a handsome return on our investment, we would be doing our own investors a disservice by not seeking a better price," said Stephen Peak, fund manager for TR European Growth (TREG), which along with other Henderson Investors' funds has a 12.77 percent interest in Forsheda.
"It has been an attractive investment for us and we are reluctant to let it go for a price that -- we feel -- does not fully reflect the true value of this company," said Peak.

British engineering firm TI Group announced the proposed acquisition of Forsheda earlier this month, a move which would make it one of the world's top three suppliers of polymer-engineered industrial seals in its chosen areas.
The Swedish polymer group recommended that shareholders accept the takeover bid, which valued it at 225 crowns per B-series share.

The offer was conditional on TI gaining control of over 90 percent of the voting rights in Forsheda, but TI said at the time it retained the right to complete the acquisition even if this condition was not fulfilled.

Forsheda's polymer engineering division comprises two core activities, sealing systems and industrial rubber, which had a turnover of 1.4 billion crowns in 1995 and posted a pre-tax profit of 224 million crowns.
